scenario: WIBTA for lying to my brother for the rest of our lives about having a disorder? | My brother who is 2 years younger than me has Aspberger's. We have known for years but it's not something that we talk about in my family because my brother is embarrassed of it in a way. He is EXTREMELY smart and always has been. He excels in math and physics and everything in between. He is going to college and taking hard classes that he does well in. Lately, he has been depressed. More than depressed. A couple of months ago, he tried to take his own life by getting drunk and swallowing a bottle of acetaminophen. He and I are extremely close and he only talks to me. He called me in a panic hours after doing this and I took him to the hospital. He went to outpatient treatment after getting discharged from inpatient. The nurse had called me and asked if my brother was diagnosed with autism ever because he shows some clear signs. I talked to my brother about it today and he is still somewhat denying that he has autism. My brother loves me to death and I love him just as much. He has always looked up to me. I can't imagine a world without him. He loves how much more alike we get as we get older. He constantly says it with a big smile on his face. I have tried to talk to him about his autism and how he shouldn't be ashamed and he should own that about himself because some people don't even realize he has bad communication skills and he's so damn smart. Occasionally, his bad communication skills are very apparent and his disorder is obvious in other ways as well. I try to tell him that people say Mark Zuckerberg and Steve Jobs have Aspberger's but it doesn't do much for him when I say that. I feel if I tell my brother I have Aspberger's as well he would learn to love it and not deny it anymore, possibly helping himself. Would I be an asshole if I live a lie for the rest of my life to make my brother feel he's not alone and possibly help him move forward in life?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to lie to my brother about having a disorder, specifically Asperger's, for the rest of our lives. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My brother is two years younger than me and has Asperger's. We've known about this for years, but it's not something we talk about in our family because he's embarrassed about it. He's extremely smart, excels in math and physics, and is doing well in college. Lately, he's been really depressed, even to the point of attempting suicide a couple of months ago. He called me in a panic, and I took him to the hospital. After that, he went through outpatient treatment. Recently, a nurse asked me if my brother was diagnosed with autism because she noticed some signs. I talked to him about it today, and he's still denying that he has autism. He loves me a lot, and I love him just as much. We've always been close, and as we've gotten older, we've become more alike, which he really likes. I've tried talking to him about his autism and how he shouldn't be ashamed of it. I've mentioned that some people think famous figures like Mark Zuckerberg and Steve Jobs have Asperger's, but that doesn't seem to help him. I'm thinking that if I told him I have Asperger's too, he might start to accept it and not deny it anymore, which could help him move forward in life. But is it right for me to lie to him about this? Would I be an asshole for doing that? I need to think about the consequences of this decision. First, lying to my brother could damage our trust. If he finds out I lied, he might feel betrayed, which could hurt our relationship. On the other hand, if telling him I have Asperger's helps him accept his own diagnosis and feel less alone, it might be worth it. I also need to consider his mental health. He's been really depressed and even attempted suicide. If lying to him helps him feel better about himself and his situation, maybe it's justified in this context. But I have to be careful not to enable his denial if that's not healthy for him. Another thing to think about is whether there's a middle ground. Maybe instead of lying, I could find another way to help him accept his diagnosis without deception. For example, I could share information about how others have embraced their autism and found strength in it. I also wonder about the long-term effects of this lie. If I tell him I have Asperger's, and he never finds out the truth, how would that affect him? Would it help him in the long run, or would it cause more confusion or issues? Additionally, I need to think about my own feelings and boundaries. Would lying to him make me uncomfortable or cause me stress? It's important to consider my own well-being in this decision as well. Maybe I should talk to a professional, like a therapist or counselor, who can provide guidance on how to approach this situation in a way that's both honest and supportive for my brother. In summary, while lying to my brother about having Asperger's might seem like a way to help him feel less alone and encourage him to accept his diagnosis, it also carries risks, such as damaging our trust and potentially enabling his denial. It might be better to find an honest and supportive way to help him accept his autism without resorting to deception.
